subject: Clarify baseline retention for raw requests vs derived outputs — Acme pilot
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 16:14:00 -0400
Subject: Pilot question — what persists by default?

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team had a follow-up: for the pilot, what does Redwood keep by default and for how long? They asked specifically about two buckets we call out internally: 1) "raw requests" (the exact request payload we send — customer text, metadata) and 2) "derived outputs" (model-generated completions, summaries, embeddings).

We need enough detail to answer our auditor: default retention windows, whether prompts vs full request bodies are treated differently, how streaming segments are handled, and whether any derived artifacts (like reranks/embeddings) are retained under the same rule or separate.

If you can share the baseline defaults (no additional retention contract) and the options to shorten that or purge on demand, that would be great. Also, if there are standard exceptions for telemetry/metrics used for infra debugging, please call those out.

Thanks,
Jane
Security Analyst — Acme Corp

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot question — what persists by default?

Jane — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise baseline we share with all pilot customers (and what applies to your current trial unless you elect stricter terms):

1) Baseline capture windows (default, no contract changes):
- Raw requests (request body including prompt text and request-level metadata): retained for 45 days by default.
- Derived outputs (model completions and immediate generation tokens): retained for 90 days by default.
- Embeddings and rerank indices: treated as derived outputs and retained for 90 days by default.

2) Prompt vs full request body: we do not separately redact prompts from the request body by default — prompts are part of the raw request capture. Customers can opt-in to a prompt-only retention mode (see option 3).

3) Options to shorten/unstore:
- Auto-purge: customers can configure an automatic purge at 7/14/30/45 days for requests and/or derived outputs.
- Prompt-only capture: for the highest privacy mode, Redwood can be configured to store only hashed prompt fingerprints (not full prompt text). This must be requested and approved before production launch.

4) Streaming segments: streaming tokens are appended to the request record as they are produced; the full request+streamed-output record follows the same retention windows above. If streaming is enabled and you choose prompt-only mode, we retain only the prompt fingerprint and final output fingerprint (not token stream).

5) Infra telemetry and debugging traces: short-lived telemetry (kernel traces, GPU scheduler logs) are retained for 30 days and are not part of the request/response capture. Separately, error payloads that include request identifiers are stored for 90 days to support incident investigation; actual request text in these error payloads follows the request retention policy above.

6) Deletion paths:
- Manual deletion API: customers can trigger ID-level deletion for specific request IDs (complies with our purge workflow; typically completes within 48 hours).
- Account-wide purge: on contract termination we run a full purge pipeline; retention metadata and tombstones may persist for auditability for an additional 30 days unless otherwise negotiated.

I'm attaching our retention matrix and a quick redline noting where pilot exceptions would be handled. If helpful, Marissa can coordinate a short call with your security team to walk through these options and record a joint action plan.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Security — Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
Attachment: redlines_acme_retention.pdf (application/pdf)

From: security@acme.com
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 14:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot question — what persists by default?

Thanks Soojin — helpful. A few clarifying points from our side before we escalate to procurement: 

- Can you confirm whether embeddings used for semantic search in our pilot would be subject to the 90-day window even if we request prompt-only capture? (we would prefer embeddings be ephemeral)
- For manual deletion: does deletion remove all downstream rerank indices and embeddings that were generated from the deleted requests, or is there a separate index-rebuild required?
- For the account-wide purge: you mention tombstones — what metadata remains in these tombstones (request id, timestamp, nothing else?), and are they searchable?

Appreciate the quick follow-up — if possible we can take the Marissa call tomorrow.

— Acme security

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, security@acme.com
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot question — what persists by default?

Jane / Acme security team — quick answers and proposed next steps: 

- Embeddings: by default they follow the derived-output 90-day retention. If you opt into prompt-only capture, we can set embeddings to a shorter TTL (default pilot option: 30 days). We will need to enable ephemeral embeddings for your dedicated pool explicitly.

- Manual deletion and downstream artifacts: our deletion workflow attempts to cascade deletes for artifacts we manage (embedding tables, rerank caches). If an embedding was exported to your environment or a third-party index, that external copy is out of scope. For internal indices we rebuild or tombstone entries; full index rebuilds are treated as a maintenance task and may take up to 72 hours depending on index size.

- Tombstones: account-wide purge leaves a minimal tombstone: request_id, deletion_timestamp, and a short audit tag indicating who authorized the purge. No prompt or output text is retained in tombstones by default, and tombstones are not searchable via the public API (only available to Redwood compliance under strict audit access).

Next steps: 1) If you want ephemeral embeddings + prompt-only capture for the pilot, I'll open a pilot change request and attach a one-page addendum to our SOW. 2) Proposed 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:00 AM ET to confirm — Marissa here; I've copied Karitk for technical details and Ben for billing impact.

Please reply with preferred call time and whether you want the pilot addendum.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
